public_sources.finding: Core SWHIDs are intrinsic content-derived identifiers; revision object identifiers are compatible with Git commit identifiers and can be looked up through Software Heritage when archived.
GET /api/1/revision/<sha1_git>/ retrieves an archived revision by a Git-compatible commit hash.
The richer provenance whereis endpoint requires authentication and special permission, and its best-context quality is not guaranteed.
The archive is conceptually append-only but explicitly supports content removal and masking.
Origins and snapshots can be removed; objects reachable only from a removed origin can become removal candidates when not referenced elsewhere.
Save Code Now is a POST/write-like archival request path and is rate-limited; relying on it would violate this child test's read-only/no-request condition.

slice.tested_scope: Official public Software Heritage documentation for SWHID/Git compatibility, revision GET lookup, provenance, archive alteration/removal, and Save Code Now request semantics. No O, downstream, other-worker state, legacy research, shared ledger, other-role receipt/config, private data, secret, POST/save request, hosted runner, external executor, manual witness, finite paid quota, scheduler mutation, wait/poll/backoff, or second leaf was used.
slice.direct_object_presence_test: not established on the available web surface; arbitrary API GET for the current own-state commit could not be directly opened through the web safety gate, and no save request was issued
reasoning: If a Git commit is already archived, its Git commit hash can deterministically address the corresponding Software Heritage revision, giving a strong independently hosted content-addressed witness with low read-only integration cost.

However, source identity alone does not guarantee that the commit has already been archived. Making an absent origin/object present would require an archival request or waiting for independent crawling, so the mechanism is not a deterministic scheduled-Chat-only no-write witness.
Software Heritage also has explicit removal/masking mechanisms, so public retrievability is not an unconditional deletion-survival guarantee.
The special provenance endpoint is permission-gated, so exact origin-context provenance cannot be required on a zero-special-permission route.

Software Heritage existing-object lookup is a strong optional independent witness only when the commit is already archived; archive presence and unconditional public retention are not guaranteed without a request/crawl and are therefore unresolved.
